To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the retrieval of atmospheric horizontal structure from a series or series of limb observations is possible, even with low S/N, and that a maximum likelihood expectation-maximization algorithm is an appropriate tool to use for this purpose.
the maximum likelihood algorithm can be used to retrieve horizontal structure from a series (of images), and that the retrieval is possible for S/N ratios of 10.

the maximum likelihood expectation maximisation (MLEM) algorithm is a good method for reconstructing atmospheric structure from satellite limb measurements, that the MLEM algorithm can reconstruct atmospheric structures with a signal to noise (S/N) ratio of 10, and that the MLEM can reconstruct both horizontal and vertical structures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a technique for retrieving the three-dimensional distribution of an atmospheric tracer from satellite observations.
the retrieval of the three-dimensional structure of the atmosphere from a series of images obtained from a satellite in a polar orbit.
the retrieval of atmospheric structure from a sequence of satellite observations, using a maximum likelihood expectation algorithm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method of retrieval from a series of images is feasible and that the method is robust with respect to observational noise.
, with a reasonable number of observations, the algorithm is able to retrieve horizontal and vertical structure in the presence of observational noise.
the algorithm developed here is capable of providing a good retrieval of horizontal structure from a series (at least 5) of limb images with a S/N ratio equal to 10.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is possible to obtain the horizontal structure from a satellite limb scan.
it is possible to reconstruct the three-dimensional structure of the atmosphere with a reasonable accuracy from the series of observations taken aboard the satellite.
it is possible, using a satellite platform, to obtain a three-dimensional image of the atmosphere.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to reconstruct the horizontal structure from a series (sequence) of observations, even if the individual observations have a relatively poor S/N.
it is possible to reconstruct the horizontal atmospheric structure using a series of limb scans, even in the presence substantial observational noise.

the maximum likelihood expectation maximisation algorithm can be used to retrieve horizontal atmospheric structure from limb images, with a S/N of 10 or greater, even if the vertical structure is known.
